artifact.self_contained_problem:
For real parameters α, β > −1 and integer n ≥ 0, let
  P_n^{(α,β)}(x) = (1/2^n) Σ_{k=0}^{n} C(n+α, n−k) C(n+β, k) (x−1)^{n−k} (x+1)^k
denote the classical Jacobi polynomial of degree n (with the standard binomial generalization C(n+γ, j) = Γ(n+γ+1)/(j!·Γ(n+γ+1−j))).

Define two associated polynomials by collecting even- and odd-order derivatives of P_n^{(α,β)} evaluated at x = 1:
  φ_n(x) := Σ_{k=0}^{⌊n/2⌋} ( (d^{2k}/dx^{2k}) P_n^{(α,β)}(x) |_{x=1} ) · x^k,
  ψ_n(x) := Σ_{k=0}^{⌊(n−1)/2⌋} ( (d^{2k+1}/dx^{2k+1}) P_n^{(α,β)}(x) |_{x=1} ) · x^k.

Assume −1 < α ≤ 1 and β > −1, so that (it is known) φ_n and ψ_n have only real, negative, simple zeros.

Prove or disprove the following two interlacing statements:
 (a) For every integer n ≥ 4, the zeros of φ_n strictly interlace the zeros of φ_{n−1}; that is, between any two consecutive zeros of φ_n there lies exactly one zero of φ_{n−1}, and vice versa where applicable.
 (b) For every integer n ≥ 4, the zeros of ψ_n strictly interlace the zeros of ψ_{n−2}.
artifact.category_tag: Zeros of orthogonal polynomials and interlacing
artifact.status_search_result: The construction of φ_n and ψ_n from derivatives at x=1 of Jacobi polynomials is due to Charalambides–Csordas–Waleffe and arises in the Jacobi tau method; reality and negativity of their zeros is known, but the interlacing of φ_n with φ_{n−1} and of ψ_n with ψ_{n−2} is posed as a conjecture/open problem. Web searches did not surface a published resolution of either interlacing claim, so the current status is unknown/likely still open.

status_evidence.title: A new property of a class of Jacobi polynomials (Charalambides–Csordas–Waleffe)
status_evidence.snippet: Polynomials whose coefficients are successive derivatives of a class of Jacobi polynomials evaluated at x=1 are stable; the paper concludes with open problems on interlacing of their zeros.
status_evidence.claim: Defines φ_n, ψ_n via derivatives at x=1 and leaves interlacing as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Spectrum of the Jacobi Tau Approximation for the Second Derivative Operator
status_evidence.snippet: Eigenvalues of the Jacobi tau method are real, negative and distinct for a range of Jacobi parameters; in the Gegenbauer case characteristic polynomials at successive orders interlace.
status_evidence.claim: Reality/negativity established, but the general interlacing of φ_n,φ_{n−1} and ψ_n,ψ_{n−2} is not proven for all admissible α,β.
